feat: recorded demo shots with a drawn cursor (Unity Recorder)

GolemShots runs scripted shots (camera views, O/C and ball keys, drags)
in game time while the Unity Recorder (com.unity.recorder 5.1.7) writes
the Game view to 1920x1080 H.264 at a constant 30 fps, so footage is
smooth however slowly the Editor renders (about 1 frame a second here
with recording on). Shots: test, stage, cabinet, laptop, toolbox,
vault, r2. A shot writes <name>.status when it ends, so a caller can
wait without querying the Editor (each query compiled C# on the main
thread and slowed recording further).

GolemCursorOverlay draws a cursor and a key badge on a screen-space
overlay the recording includes: scripted drags move no real cursor.
GolemAudit's drag places it each step; BestGrab/GrabPoint expose where
a drag grabs, so the cursor can glide there first.

All seven clips recorded at their scripted lengths (within 0.03 s).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: choices file (golem_auto.py), import from any folder; two cutter fixes

golem_auto.py is GOLEM's choice step as a file: a JSON with who chose
(source), the splitter (cut / parts), the lid or part roles and joints,
optional size and density; it runs golem_cutter.py or golem_assemble.py
and copies the choices next to the output. Today the artist writes it;
it is the slot a vision model fills. Roles lid*, door*, drawer* get
default joints.

GolemMenu: ImportFolder(dir) and GOLEM > Import Folder... import split
props from any folder into the open scene without saving, frame them,
and report masses and joints; SizeFor falls back to the choices file's
size_m and density when golem_sizes.json has no entry.

R2 rehearsal (in the dummy_arcade sandbox, nothing generated): a laptop
GOLEM had never processed went through the Hyper3D Unity bridge's own
loader (RodinModel.LoadModel; saved as Assets/<id>/<md5>_base.glb, 1
renderer, 0 physics components), golem_auto.py (4.6 s), ImportFolder
(1.42 + 0.33 kg, hinge -110.5..22.5 deg), self-test PASS, and in Play
it drags shut and open on the floor, 0 reversals.

It found two cutter bugs on this thin-decked laptop, both --open-part
only:
- Raised keys poking above the cut went with the screen; its convex
  collider spanned them and hit the floor at -6 deg. Loose pieces of the
  open part more than 3% of the model's size away from it now go back
  to the body (2 pieces, 191 vertices here; none for the demo laptop),
  and their cut points no longer skew the hinge. The measured opening
  angle corrected from 120.2 to 112.5 deg.
- The hinge sat at the back of the screen's 2 cm-thick edge, so closing
  swung the front edge 2 cm below it: through a 1.5 cm deck into the
  floor at -44 deg (and a closed screen sinks its thickness into the
  deck). Open parts now turn about the front of their cut edge.
  The demo laptop's pivot moves 0.11 units forward (axis and limits
  unchanged); demo scene rebuilt: self-test 8/8 PASS, O/C stable, no
  prop below the floor.

The edit-mode self-test can't catch floor problems: it simulates a copy
50 m away, off the ground.

feat: vault close-up from the hinge side, showing the hinge arm

The close-up picker avoided a side hinge's own side, since from there
an open door stands across its doorway. For a door hung from hinge
hardware (golem_hinge_* objects, from golem_assemble.py --hinge-arms)
that hid the arm behind the open door, so such props now prefer their
hinge side, weighted 15: enough to outweigh one sight line grazing a
neighbour's swept box (the vault's hinge side grazes the cabinet's
pulled-out drawers), not two. Props without hardware keep the old rule.

Vault scores: hinge side 10, far side 15 -> hinge side. Captured
closed, mid-swing and open: the barrel and arm stay in shot and the
cabinet doesn't cover the vault. README vault image retaken.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: vault door hangs from an offset hinge arm

Problem, measured with mid-height cross-sections: the hinge axis sat on
the door's bounding-box corner, where its front-most point (the central
locking hub) meets its side, so the axis floated ~0.1 m in front of the
door's rim and the open door stood ~0.2 m off the frame with nothing
joining them. Moving the axis onto the rim can't make a round door
flush (it meets a vertical line at one point only) and swings its thick
seated back into the ring.

golem_assemble.py gets --hinge-arms, as on a real round vault door: the
axis goes beside the frame (the root body's extreme toward HINGE and
toward OPENS, centered on the part along the hinge line), and two
separate objects are built: a hinge barrel on that axis, part of the
body, and an arm, part of the door (a bar in front of the frame's face
plus a foot down to the recessed door face). Axis direction and limits
are unchanged; the pivot moves from (-0.738, -0.056, 0.263) to
(-0.950, -0.056, 0.309), glTF frame.

Unity (no articulator changes): the hardware imports as golem_hinge_*
children with their own colliders and mass; the wall builder leaves
it out when sizing the round doorway. Self-test PASS; the door swings
0-100-0 deg with the frame at 0.00 deg; across the swing the door and
arm stay at least 7.1 cm from the wall face.

Side effects, stated: the vault's 2.20 m size now includes the barrel,
so it scales down 2.6% and its masses read 1,618 + 2,695 kg (the
meshes are open, so their volume also shifts with the moved origin).
From the right-hand close-up the open door hides the arm and stands
0.3-0.45 m out from the frame. A ring-band measurement showed no
clipping difference between the old and new axis. METRICS.md not
re-run for this recipe change.

README: vault figures, recipe, manifest example and images updated.

feat: drawer boxes behind the cabinet's sliding fronts

Generated models draw drawers as front panels only, so a pulled-out
drawer was a floating board. golem_assemble.py gets --drawer-boxes:
behind every --slide part it builds an open-top box (bottom, two sides,
back) into the part's own mesh, after the joint is computed, so pivot,
axis and travel still come from the front alone (the cabinet's joint
fields are byte-identical to before).

Box: from the front's back face into the body, 1.25x the travel deep
(capped at 95% of the space behind the front), 92% of the front's
width, 80% of its height, walls 2% of its width; slabs don't overlap,
so the mesh volume counts each wall once. Material: a plain colour
taken from the front's texture (area-weighted median at each face's UV
centre, sRGB to linear), so the metal handle doesn't tint it.

Unity (no code changes): each drawer has one convex collider spanning
front and box (0.70 x 0.67 m); masses from the unchanged volume rule
are now 1.5-1.6 kg, and 4.5 kg for the bottom drawer, whose carved
front is open fragments, so its volume estimate is looser.
Self-test 8/8 PASS; O/C: all four slide 0.49 m, cabinet tilt 0.00 deg;
scripted drag of the bottom drawer: 0 reversals, 2 px cursor miss.

METRICS.md regenerated (4.1-4.9 s per prop; untouched props also
moved 0.2-0.4 s, so part of the change is run-to-run variance);
README numbers, cabinet row, limits line and cabinet image updated.

feat: fourth cabinet drawer, camera presets, toolbox shot first

Fourth drawer: BANG drew four drawer fronts on the filing cabinet but
split out only three; the bottom front was 242 loose pieces inside the
carcass part (root.7). golem_assemble.py gets --carve NEW=SOURCE:box,

each prop in line order; the camera glides between them. GolemStage
fits each close-up to everything the prop's parts sweep through
between their limits, and picks the side (30 deg left or right) whose
sight lines pass through fewer neighbours, then the side away from a
side hinge, so the open vault door does not stand across its doorway.
Checked by captures of every view with all parts open.

Ball: the toolbox shot fires first (it tips the 17 kg toolbox onto its
side); the anchored vault's shot only shows the door holding.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: stop props tipping over when parts move; drag that never inverts

Measured with a new play-mode audit (GolemAudit: records tilt, slide and
joint travel; scripts O, C, ball shots and drags through the same code
the keys and mouse use).

Before, O then C on the demo stage: every part covered 90% of its travel
in 0.25 s whatever its mass (peaks 415-1100 deg/s, drawers 3.3 m/s). The
vault frame tipped to 125 deg and lay flat; the chest fell on its back
(89 deg); toolbox and laptop rocked 9-11 deg.

- O/C and drags set a goal; the drive target follows a trapezoidal
  profile (0.3 s ramps) at a top speed falling as 1/sqrt(mass), clamped
  to 25-120 deg/s or 0.15-0.6 m/s, fed to the drive as target velocity.
- Drives are acceleration drives (scaled by each joint's inertia, 10 Hz,
  critically damped) instead of force gains scaled by mass, which left
  the heavy chest lid trailing its target and hitting its limit.
- Each root part gets a flat footprint collider. Generated bases are not
  flat: the chest rocked from one hull facet to another as its lid's
  weight moved back.
- The vault door is anchored ("anchored" in golem_sizes.json): its 2.8 t
  door outweighs its 1.7 t frame, so free-standing it topples.

After: max tilt vault 0.00, chest 0.27, toolbox 0.43, laptop 0.07,
cabinet 0.00 deg; all props now stand level at rest.

Drag: the screen mapping is fixed at the grab (the chord between the
grabbed point's positions at the joint's two limits) instead of being
recomputed every frame, which flipped sign where the laptop screen's
path turns toward the camera. 35 scripted drags from 4 viewpoints all
moved the right way with 0 reversals; the grabbed point ends 0-23 px
from the cursor, the vault door 19-76 px (straight chord, curved arc).

Self-test: 7/7 PASS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: measured pipeline metrics for the pitch

golem_metrics.py times each stage per prop and writes METRICS.md:
Hyper3D cloud time from each job's record (submitted -> downloaded),
GOLEM's split replayed and timed (Blender start-up measured
separately), and a timed Unity rebuild with fresh glTFast imports.

Measured on the i5-11320H laptop:
- GOLEM's own work per prop: 4.5-5.7 s (2.3 s of it Blender start-up);
  Unity import + joints 0.57-0.74 s per prop.
- Hyper3D: 85-125 s per Rodin generation, 283-311 s per BANG split;
  0.5 credits per job.
- End to end: about 1.5-2 min per prop with the Blender cutter,
  6-9 min with BANG.

golem_props.json records how each prop was made (its Hyper3D jobs and
the artist's split choices) so the metrics can replay them.
GolemMenu.TimedRebuild writes its timings to a file as well, because
fresh imports outlast the Pipeline server's 5 s main-thread wait.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: demo stage, physics-proof ball, and masses from real mesh volume

- Mass = effective density x enclosed mesh volume (signed tetrahedra,
  world scale), falling back to half the bounding box only for meshes
  too open to trust. The box estimate made an open laptop screen
  heavier than its base. Now: laptop 3.0 + 0.9 kg, toolbox 11.9 + 5.0,
  chest 30 + 15.7, cabinet 59.6 + 3 x 0.5, vault frame 1718 + door
  2811. golem_sizes.json densities are effective values for hollow
  objects (wooden chest 150, sheet-steel toolbox 350, cast-iron vault
  3000...).
- GolemStage (GOLEM > Build Demo Stage): presentation line from
  smallest to largest; props become free physics bodies on the floor;
  dark floor and backdrop (the backdrop Quad is turned to face the
  camera); key and fill lights; 30-degree camera fitted to the line.
  Capture() renders the camera straight to a PNG at 16:9, because the
  Editor's tiled screenshot misaligned and drew props twice.
- GolemBallLauncher: a 30 kg ball, 7 m/s. It fires at the vault door
  1.5 s after Play; V / T / B repeat the vault, toolbox and cabinet
  shots. Measured in Play mode: vault door (4.5 t) did not move;
  toolbox (17 kg) knocked 0.57 m and flipped 140 degrees; cabinet
  (61 kg) shoved 3.5 cm.
- Fix an Editor crash: re-importing a model while its old instance
  was in the scene swapped meshes under articulation colliders and
  PhysX crashed in detachShape. The old instance is now removed
  first, and unchanged models aren't re-imported at all.
- Self-test pins its test copies, since props are now free bodies.
  GolemMenu.RebuildAll() = import + self-test + stage.
- Player setting Run In Background on, so Play mode keeps simulating
  while the Editor is unfocused (driven by an agent).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: scale props to real-world size and give parts real mass

golem_sizes.json sets each prop's largest dimension and an effective
density: chest 0.90 m, toolbox 0.55 m, laptop 0.36 m, vault door
2.20 m, filing cabinet 1.30 m. On import, Unity scales each prop
uniformly to that size before building joints; slide travel scales
with it (drawers 0.71 -> 0.34 m); each part's mass is density x half
its bounding box; joint motor strength grows with mass so heavy parts
still move. All 7 joints pass the self-test at real scale.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Scene now: chest, toolbox, laptop, vault door, filing cabinet; all 7

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: BANG assembler, open-part cutting, and a stricter seam rule

Batch of four Rodin props plus a BANG split (credits: 5 generations at
0.5 each, Medium and High alike; BANG via the CLI 0.5, not the web
UI's 10).

- golem_assemble.py (tier 1 adapter): turns a multi-part model such as
  BANG output into a GOLEM split. The caller picks the fixed part, the
  moving group, its hinge side and which way it opens; the script puts
  the pivot on the group's box at the hinge edge and on the side it
  opens toward, sets axis = cross(-hinge, opens) so positive rotation
  opens it, and writes the same .glb + joints JSON as the cutter. Runs
  in Blender, so BANG's textures survive. Vault door: frame fixed,
  door swings on its left edge toward the front.
- golem_cutter.py:
  - a seam needs real geometry on both sides (each side at least half
    the median section): the toolbox's handle legs had won as a
    "groove"; the cut now finds the lid rim (0.875 -> 0.584);
  - --open-part for parts that come already open (Rodin made both
    "closed" laptop prompts open): cut where the section levels off
    above the deck (not mid-keycap), measure how far the part stands
    open from its cross-section, and set limits from almost closed to
    135 degrees (laptop: stands at 107 deg, limits -105..28);
  - the joint JSON now records rest_deg and outward (the hinge side,
    toward which positive rotation moves the part).
- golem_preview.py: opens every moving part named in the joints JSON,
  not just "lid", and resolves the output folder (Blender misreads
  relative render paths).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: Unity 6.6 project that turns split props into ArticulationBody joints

GolemUnity (URP, created headlessly with the Unity CLI) with glTFast
6.20.0 pinned in the package manifest.

- GolemArticulator: builds the ArticulationBody chain from a prop's
  *_joints.json. glTFast mirrors X (M = diag(-1, 1, 1)); points and
  slides map with M, rotation axes with -M = (x, -y, -z), so the same
  angle opens the part the same way. The anchor sits on the pivot with
  its X axis (Unity's joint axis) along the hinge; the root part is
  immovable; drives hold the limits; parts get convex colliders.
- GolemJointLink: ignores collisions between a part and its parent,
  whose colliders overlap along the seam.
- GolemDragController: drag a part with the mouse (up opens), O opens
  everything, C closes; joints move through their drives.
- GOLEM menu: Import Split Props (from ../assets/split) and Run Hinge
  Self-Test. BuildFromCommandLine does both headlessly and saves
  SampleScene. glTFast folds a glTF's single root node into the import
  and renames it after the file, so each prop sits under a wrapper that
  stands in for the glTF scene root, and a root part that isn't found
  by name is the import's top object.
- Self-test: drive each joint to 70 degrees in a scripted simulation
  and require the part to turn and rise; it now fails when it finds no
  joints (the first run passed with nothing to test). Chest result:
  turned 70.0 deg, rose 0.407 -> PASS.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: generate via the Hyper3D CLI, cut real Rodin chests at their seam

First real asset: a Rodin Gen-2.5 treasure chest (50k faces, 106 s,
0.5 credits) cut at its true lid seam and opened about the right hinge.

- hyper3d_client.py: drive the official @hyper3d/cli (browser sign-in)
  instead of the REST API, whose keys are locked to Hyper3D's Business
  tier. Runs the CLI's JS entry through Node directly, so cmd.exe can't
  reinterpret quotes or '&' in prompts. Adds `bang` (split with an
  instruction such as "separate the lid") and `auth`. Saves Rodin's PBR
  model as <name>.glb and other variants as <name>_<variant>.glb.
- golem_cutter.py, three fixes found on the real chest:
  - weld before cutting: glTF import splits vertices along UV seams,
    which left every cut outline open and uncapped (0/2 -> 9/9 caps);
  - find the seam from the exact cross-section area (outline oriented
    by face normals, shoelace sum) instead of the bounding-box
    footprint, which brackets and the hasp kept flat across the gap
    (auto cut 0.904 -> 0.592; the seam is at ~0.60 by eye);
  - give the caps a plain interior material instead of a smeared
    texture.
- golem_preview.py: render a .glb in headless Blender (front, side,
  three-quarter, textured), with optional height marks for choosing a
  seam and an --open-deg check that swings the lid about its hinge.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat: add the Hyper3D Rodin client and the Blender tier-2 cutter

- hyper3d_client.py: text prompt -> Rodin Gen-2.5 job -> poll -> .glb in
  assets/raw/. Records each job in <name>.job.json as soon as it is
  accepted (task uuid, subscription key, credits) so an interrupted run
  can be resumed without paying twice. Polls from 5 s, backing off to
  30 s, honoring Retry-After, as the API docs ask. `ping` checks the
  key with a dummy status query and spends no credits.
- golem_secrets.py: reads keys from ~/.golem/secrets.env, outside the
  repo; real environment variables win; values are never printed.
- golem_cutter.py: relaunches itself in headless Blender 5.2, joins the
  mesh, and cuts it with a horizontal plane into body + lid, capping both
  cuts. It finds the seam from cross-section footprints: a groove (lower
  than both sides, cut at its middle) ranks above a lip (a step); with
  neither it falls back to 70% of the height. The hinge sits on the seam
  outline at the chosen side; the lid is a child of the body with its
  origin on the hinge. Writes the split .glb plus a joint JSON in glTF
  coordinates, with every seam candidate for a model to choose from.
- tests/test_cutter.py: groove, overhanging lid and plain box chests,
  checking the cut height, hinge position, axis, hierarchy and capped
  (watertight) parts.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
